annotation.title_clean: Opinion of the European Economic and Social Committee – Regulatory simplification – The use of digital tools in better law-making (Exploratory opinion requested by the Danish Presidency)
annotation.title_en: Opinion of the European Economic and Social Committee – Regulatory simplification – The use of digital tools in better law-making (Exploratory opinion requested by the Danish Presidency)
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union, C/2025/5146
named_instruments_referenced: Czech Act No 222/2016 on the Collection of Laws
annotation.summary_en: Exploratory EESC opinion, requested by the Danish Presidency, recommending that EU institutions use AI and digital tools to simplify regulation and improve law-making. It proposes a unified interoperable legislative platform, summaries of obligations for each legal act, and AI-driven consistency checks. AI use should stay human-centric, be properly tested, and not replace stakeholder dialogue. The opinion does not cover robotics.
key_provisions_or_claims: Attach a structured, human-translated summary of obligations to every new EU legal act and to existing legislation
Establish a unified interoperable digital EU law-making platform via an updated interinstitutional agreement
Appoint a regtech chief to introduce AI and digital tools in EU regulatory processes
AI must be thoroughly tested to avoid bias and cannot replace dialogue with stakeholders and social partners
Create a centralised obligations database and EU data spaces under the once-only principle
